name: Liangzhu culture
title: The story of the Liangzhu culture

text: More than 5,000 years ago, the Liangzhu people lived by the Yangtze River in eastern China.
Their land was full of rivers, so many houses stood on stilts, safe from floods.
src: c. 3300 BCE: The Liangzhu culture emerges in the Yangtze River Delta / The Yangtze River Delta and the Taihu Lake area of eastern China
a plain of rivers / Houses were often raised on stilts over rivers or shorelines as protection against floods

text: They grew rice in wet fields, brought water to their crops and farmed fish.
Their biggest city had clay walls with six gates, and probably dams against floods.
src: The economy rested on advanced agriculture, with irrigation, paddy rice and aquaculture
Its clay walls enclosed 290 hectares and had six gates / about 8 km to the north lay dam-like works thought to be a flood-protection system

text: Rich people were buried with jade, silk and ivory, but poorer people mostly with pots.
Jade carvers made tubes called cong and flat discs called bi.
src: Jade, silk, ivory and lacquer objects have been found only in elite burials, while poorer graves held mostly pottery
cong, the tube-shaped cylinders / bi discs

text: About 4,300 years ago, heavy rain and floods probably drove them from their land.
Their jade shaped later Chinese art, and their city’s ruins are now protected by UNESCO.
src: after c. 2300 BCE: The culture disappears from the Taihu Lake area, probably after decades of heavy rain and flooding

Liangzhu jade work is said to have influenced ritual objects in later Chinese culture / The site is now protected and on display / the archaeological ruins of Liangzhu City were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
